title: Four-Dimensional Adventure
description: Count how many constellations form among 4D points connected by Manhattan distance ≤ 3.
writeup:
## Approach

The puzzle can be modeled as a graph problem. Each 4‑dimensional point is a node, and an edge exists between two points if their Manhattan distance is at most 3. A constellation is simply a connected component in this graph. Because the number of points is manageable, a straightforward DFS or BFS from each unvisited point efficiently identifies all components.

## Part 1

For each point, we check which other points lie within distance 3. Starting from any unvisited point, we perform a depth‑first search to mark all points reachable through chains of close neighbors. Each DFS corresponds to one constellation. Counting how many times we initiate a DFS gives the total number of constellations.

## Part 2

This puzzle has no second part. The answer to Part 2 is intentionally left empty.
